name: Qwen3.5 2B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Only 6 of 24 layers (every 4th) use full attention with a growing KV cache; the 18 Gated DeltaNet layers keep a fixed-size state.

good_for: Reads photos and short videos on phones and cheap laptops, and understands about 200 languages.
weak_at: Too small to handle long multi-step tasks reliably.
notes: Image and video reading is built into the download. Needs a recent version of llama.cpp or Ollama with Qwen3.5 support. Unsloth also offers compact files that predict several words at once, for faster replies.

name: Qwen3.5 4B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: 8 of 32 layers use full attention; the 24 Gated DeltaNet layers keep a fixed-size state that does not grow with context.

good_for: A small model for simple assistants that use tools, read images and work through long documents.
weak_at: Knows fewer facts than bigger models.
notes: It thinks before answering by default; switch thinking off for quick answers. It reads up to 262,000 tokens as standard, and about 1 million with an extension setting. Needs a recent version of llama.cpp or Ollama with Qwen3.5 support.

name: Gemma 4 E2B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: 7 of 35 layers are global (head_dim 512, 1 KV head); the last 20 layers reuse KV from earlier layers, so only 3 global layers store a growing cache. Sliding layers (512-token window, head_dim 256) add a fixed ~6 MB.

good_for: Runs on a phone and understands spoken audio and pictures as well as typed text.
weak_at: Struggles with harder reasoning and programming.
notes: About 2.3 billion of its 5.1 billion parameters do the work for each word; the rest is a lookup table that can stay on the SSD. Google publishes its own 4-bit version made to keep quality close to the original (Ollama tag gemma4:e2b-it-qat).

name: Gemma 4 E4B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: 7 of 42 layers are global (head_dim 512, 2 KV heads); the last 18 layers reuse earlier KV, so 4 global layers store a growing cache. Sliding layers (512-token window) add a fixed ~21 MB.

good_for: An offline assistant for laptops and phones that takes voice, pictures and text; NVIDIA built a voice assistant on it.
weak_at: Limited at programming and longer multi-step jobs.
notes: About 4.5 billion of its 8 billion parameters do the work for each word; the rest is a lookup table that can stay on the SSD. Google publishes its own 4-bit version made to keep quality close to the original (Ollama tag gemma4:e4b-it-qat).

name: LFM3 1.7B
license_note: Free for commercial use only if your organisation's yearly revenue is under US$10 million; larger companies need a paid licence from Liquid AI.

arch_detail.kv_note: Tri-hybrid: 13 short-convolution layers (tiny fixed state), 5 sliding-window layers (256 tokens, fixed ~5 MB) and 6 full-attention layers that carry the growing cache.

good_for: Very quick at using tools and filling in structured forms, and easy to retrain on your own data.
weak_at: Companies with more than US$10 million revenue a year must pay for a licence.
notes: Runs in llama.cpp, Ollama and LM Studio from Liquid AI's own compact files, and supports 16 languages, including German but not Swedish. It thinks before answering by default, and Liquid says switching that off can give uneven results. Liquid does not recommend it for coding on its own, and suggests letting it look facts up in your documents.

name: Granite 4.2 3B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Plain transformer: every layer stores K and V (8 KV heads x 64 dims).

good_for: A small business model for answering questions from your own documents, with neatly structured output.
weak_at: Reads text only, not images.
notes: IBM publishes its own compact files as well as 8-bit and 4-bit versions. It reads 128,000 tokens as standard, and IBM says this can be extended to 512,000. Thinking can be set to full, low or off.

name: Ministral 3 3B Instruct
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Every layer stores K and V; no sliding window.

good_for: A tiny European model that reads images and writes well in the main European languages.
weak_at: Answers straight away, with no step-by-step reasoning mode.
notes: The released files are already 8-bit, so higher precision settings add nothing. Mistral publishes its own compact files. A separate Reasoning version that thinks before answering is also available.

name: Qwen3.5 9B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: 8 of 32 layers use full attention; the 24 Gated DeltaNet layers keep a fixed-size state.

good_for: One of the most capable models that run on an ordinary laptop, and it also reads images and video.
weak_at: Thinks at length before answering, so simple questions feel slow.
notes: It thinks before answering by default; switch thinking off for ordinary chat. Needs a recent version of llama.cpp or Ollama with Qwen3.5 support. Unsloth also offers compact files that predict several words at once, for faster replies.

name: Gemma 4 12B Unified
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: 8 of 48 layers are global (1 KV head x 512 dims). 40 sliding layers (1024-token window, 8 KV heads x 256) add a fixed ~336 MB at FP16. Global layers reuse K as V (attention_k_eq_v); runtimes that exploit this need half the global cache.

good_for: Listens to audio and looks at images directly; often recommended for writing and chat on mid-range graphics cards.
weak_at: Less capable than Qwen at programming on its own.
notes: Images and audio go straight into the main model, with no separate image or audio part. Google publishes its own 4-bit version made to keep quality close to the original (Ollama tag gemma4:12b-it-qat). Whether llama.cpp and Ollama pass audio to this model has not been tested.

name: Ministral 3 14B Instruct
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Every layer stores K and V.

good_for: Mistral's mid-size model from France, good at European languages and at reading images.
weak_at: Older release with no step-by-step reasoning mode.
notes: The released files are already 8-bit, so higher precision settings add nothing. Mistral publishes its own compact files, and a separate Reasoning version thinks before answering. Its listed languages include German, French, Dutch, Italian, Spanish and Portuguese.

name: Granite 4.2 8B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Plain transformer: every layer stores K and V.

good_for: A business assistant for searching your own documents and using tools, tested in German and eleven other languages.
weak_at: Reads text only, not images.
notes: IBM publishes its own compact files as well as 8-bit and 4-bit versions.

name: Olmo 3 7B Instruct
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: 8 of 32 layers are full attention with 32 KV heads (no GQA). The 24 sliding layers (4096-token window) add a fixed ~1.6 GB at FP16 once context passes 4K.

good_for: Fully open: its training data and code are public, so you can see exactly how it was made.
weak_at: Less capable than other models of the same size.
notes: A separate Think version reasons before answering. Long conversations need more memory than with most 7B models.

name: EuroLLM 9B Instruct (2512)
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Llama-style transformer; every layer stores K and V.

good_for: Translates and writes in all official EU languages, Swedish and German included, on modest hardware.
weak_at: Cannot use tools and only handles medium-length documents.
notes: It uses the standard Llama design, so any version of llama.cpp runs it. There are no official compact files; the ones linked here come from a community uploader (mradermacher). Ollama's library does not include it; you can import the compact file into Ollama yourself.

name: Apertus 1.5 8B
lab: Swiss AI Initiative (EPFL, ETH Zurich, CSCS)
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Same language-model architecture as Apertus 1.0 (32 layers, 8 KV heads); values taken from the 1.0 config because the 1.5 config sits behind a click-through gate.

good_for: A fully open Swiss model trained only on data whose owners did not opt out, covering very many languages.
weak_at: No ready-made download for common local apps yet.
notes: You must accept the terms on Hugging Face before downloading; approval is automatic. Version 1.5 adds image and audio input, and it is not confirmed that llama.cpp supports it yet. The older text-only Apertus 1.0 has compact files from Unsloth.

name: Qwen3.8 27B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: 16 of 64 layers use full attention; the 48 Gated DeltaNet layers keep a fixed-size state.

good_for: The strongest model here for one 24 GB graphics card, and very good at fixing bugs in real projects by itself.
weak_at: Replies more slowly than similar-size models built for speed.
notes: It is built the same way as Qwen3.5, so llama.cpp versions that run Qwen3.5 also run this one. It thinks before answering by default, and you can set how much it thinks. The many "uncensored" copies on Hugging Face are edits by other people and do not come from Qwen.

name: Qwen3.6 35B-A3B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: 10 of 40 layers use full attention (2 KV heads); the rest are Gated DeltaNet with fixed state. 256 experts, 8 routed + 1 shared per token.

good_for: A quick coding helper that stays fast even when part of it has to run on the main processor.
weak_at: Needs memory for its full size, and is less capable than Qwen3.8 27B.
notes: Still the newest Qwen of this size; there is no Qwen3.8 version. Qwen advises a context length of at least 128,000 tokens to keep its reasoning quality. Ollama also has a coding tag (qwen3.6:35b-a3b-coding).

name: Gemma 4 31B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: 10 of 60 layers are global (4 KV heads x 512). 50 sliding layers (1024-token window, 16 KV heads x 256) add a fixed ~840 MB at FP16. Global layers reuse K as V; a runtime that exploits this halves the growing part.

good_for: Writes natural-sounding text that people rate highly in blind comparisons, and is strong at maths and science.
weak_at: Clearly weaker than Qwen at programming tasks it does on its own.
notes: Google publishes its own 4-bit version made to keep quality close to the original (Ollama tag gemma4:31b-it-qat). Even a short chat needs about 0.84 GB of conversation memory on top of the model.

name: Gemma 4 26B-A4B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: 5 of 30 layers are global (2 KV heads x 512). 25 sliding layers (1024-token window) add a fixed ~210 MB. 128 experts, 8 active + 1 shared.

good_for: Gemma 4 quality with replies about as quick as a small model; a good chat model for 16-24 GB machines.
weak_at: Understands images but not audio, unlike the smaller Gemmas.
notes: Google publishes its own 4-bit version made to keep quality close to the original (Ollama tag gemma4:26b-a4b-it-qat). The size includes an image-reading part of about 0.55 billion parameters.

name: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B
license_note: Permissive: commercial use is allowed with no limits on revenue or user numbers. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Mamba-2 hybrid: only 6 of 52 blocks are attention (2 KV heads); 23 Mamba-2 blocks keep a fixed state and 23 are MoE feed-forward. KV grows very slowly with context.

good_for: Made for assistants that run all day; its memory use stays low even in very long conversations.
weak_at: Officially supports only six languages, and Swedish is not one of them.
notes: Standard llama.cpp appears to support it, since the llama.cpp team publishes compact files for it. NVIDIA also offers a 4-bit version for its newest graphics cards (Blackwell generation, such as the RTX 50 series). The supported languages are English, Spanish, French, German, Italian and Japanese.

name: Muse Glimmer 30B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Local/local/local/global pattern: 13 of 52 layers are global; 39 sliding layers (2048-token window) add a fixed ~82 MB. Only 2 KV heads, so the cache is small for a dense 30B.

good_for: Meta's model for local assistants that use many tools, recover from their own mistakes and read long documents.
weak_at: Weaker than Qwen at typing terminal commands and operating a computer.
notes: You set how much it thinks (low, medium, high or extra high) in the system prompt, the standing instructions at the start of a chat; there is no documented way to switch thinking off. Meta publishes its own compact files, which include an image-reading part of about 1.8 billion parameters.

name: gpt-oss 20B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Alternating layers: 12 full-attention and 12 sliding (128-token window, fixed ~3 MB). 32 experts, 4 active.

good_for: Careful step-by-step reasoning for maths and logic that fits in 16 GB and runs in every popular local app.
weak_at: Always thinks before answering, and users often find its creative writing flat.
notes: The released files are already 4-bit (about 13 GB), so higher precision settings add nothing and compact files barely shrink it. You can set how much it thinks: low, medium or high. OpenAI had released no newer open model as of November 2026.

name: Devstral Small 2 24B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Every layer stores K and V.

good_for: Mistral's coding assistant that finds its way around large projects and edits many files at once.
weak_at: No step-by-step reasoning mode, and newer Qwen models fix more bugs.
notes: The released files are already 8-bit, so higher precision settings add nothing. Mistral states a context length of 256,000 tokens; some tools list a higher limit.

name: Granite 4.2 30B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Plain transformer: every layer stores K and V.

good_for: IBM's largest Granite, for using tools and answering from company documents, with support available from IBM.
weak_at: Reads text only, and is slower than similar-size models built for speed.
notes: IBM publishes its own compact files as well as 8-bit and 4-bit versions. Long conversations take more memory than with the other mid-size models here.

name: Olmo 3.1 32B Instruct
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: 16 of 64 layers are full attention; 48 sliding layers (4096-token window) add a fixed ~805 MB once context passes 4K.

good_for: The most capable fully open model, with its data and training code public, suited to research and audits.
weak_at: Handles shorter documents and is less capable than rivals with private training data.
notes: A separate Think version reasons before answering (Ollama tag olmo-3.1:32b-think).

name: EuroLLM 22B Instruct (2512)
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Llama-style transformer; every layer stores K and V.

good_for: An EU-funded model that translates well between all official EU languages, including Swedish and German.
weak_at: Cannot use tools and only handles medium-length documents.
notes: It uses the standard Llama design, so any version of llama.cpp runs it. Ollama's library does not include it; you can import the compact files into Ollama yourself.

name: Nemotron 3 Nano Omni 30B-A3B
license_note: Commercial use is allowed with no revenue limits. Keep NVIDIA's notices; your licence ends if you sue claiming the model infringes your rights.

arch_detail.kv_note: Mamba-2 hybrid: 6 of 52 blocks are attention (2 KV heads); Mamba blocks keep a fixed state.

good_for: Watches videos with their sound, writes down speech and reads documents and charts, all in one model.
weak_at: Built on NVIDIA's older generation of text model.
notes: NVIDIA also offers an 8-bit version (33 GB) and a 4-bit version. The Ollama model nemotron-3-nano:30b is a different, text-only model. Check that your software accepts audio and video input; text and images are the safest choice.

name: Qwen3.8 Flash-Next (125B-A6B)
license_note: Commercial use is allowed, but any company that offers AI models as an online service or sells an AI coding or office assistant needs a separate licence from Qwen. Products with more than 100 million monthly users or US$20 million monthly revenue must show the model name.

arch_detail.kv_note: 12 of 48 layers use Qwen Sparse Attention with 2 KV heads; 36 Gated DeltaNet layers keep fixed state. A small sparse-attention indexer key (128 dims, 4x compressed) is cached per token on those 12 layers (~0.8 KB/token extra).

good_for: An early version of Qwen's next design. Good at fixing code by itself, and it still replies quickly.
weak_at: Companies that sell AI access or coding assistants need a separate licence deal.
notes: The 180B figure includes a 51B lookup table that can stay on the SSD; the part that has to sit in fast memory is about 129B. Keeping the table on the SSD needs a recent version of llama.cpp. In Ollama, use the full tag (qwen3.8-flash-next:125b-a6b-q4_K_M), because there is no default tag.

name: Qwen3.5 122B-A10B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: 12 of 48 layers use full attention (2 KV heads); the rest are Gated DeltaNet with fixed state. 256 experts, 8 routed + 1 shared.

good_for: The largest freely licensed Qwen that fits a 128 GB computer, balanced across images, code and many languages.
weak_at: Newer Qwen3.8 models are better at programming.
notes: Qwen publishes an official 4-bit version for server software such as vLLM and SGLang. For companies that cannot accept the licence of Qwen3.8 Flash-Next, this is the freely licensed choice that needs about the same memory.

name: gpt-oss 120B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Alternating layers: 18 full-attention and 18 sliding (128-token window, fixed ~5 MB). 128 experts, 4 active.

good_for: Very strong at contest-style maths and programming puzzles, with quick replies for its size.
weak_at: Weak at fixing bugs in large real-world software projects by itself.
notes: The released files are already 4-bit (about 61 GB), so higher precision settings add nothing. That fits a single 80 GB graphics card, or a Mac or AMD Strix Halo computer with 96 to 128 GB of memory. You can set how much it thinks: low, medium or high.

name: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B-A12B
license_note: Permissive: commercial use is allowed with no limits on revenue or user numbers. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Mamba-2 hybrid: 8 of 88 blocks are attention (2 KV heads); 40 Mamba-2 blocks keep fixed state; 40 LatentMoE blocks (512 experts, 22 active).

good_for: NVIDIA's model for reading documents, charts and code, and it stays cheap to run on very long inputs.
weak_at: Scores lower on general tests of ability than other models of its size.
notes: NVIDIA offers a 4-bit version for DGX Spark and its newest (Blackwell) graphics cards. It has a built-in part that predicts several words at once, which some software uses to reply faster. Standard llama.cpp appears to support it, since the llama.cpp team publishes compact files for it.

name: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B
license_note: Permissive: commercial use is allowed with no limits on revenue or user numbers. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Same hybrid layout as Super VL: 8 of 88 blocks are attention (2 KV heads), the rest Mamba-2 or MoE (240 experts per layer, 9 active).

good_for: Squeezes a large model into 24 GB of graphics memory for everyday assistant tasks with pictures and video.
weak_at: Nobody has independently checked how much its heavy compression costs in quality.
notes: The "24GB" release is already 2-bit (about 24.6 GB) and was trained at that precision. Do not make your own 2-bit version from the full 16-bit files (about 150 GB); use NVIDIA's 24GB files or the Ollama tag (25 GB).

name: Mistral Small 4 119B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Multi-head latent attention: each layer caches one 256-dim latent plus a 64-dim RoPE key (320 values) instead of full K and V. 128 experts, 4 active + 1 shared.

good_for: A freely licensed European all-rounder that can answer at once or think first, and replies quickly for its size.
weak_at: Not in Ollama, and needs about 70 GB of memory.
notes: The released files are already 8-bit (about 119 GB), so higher precision settings add nothing; Mistral also publishes a 4-bit version. Thinking can be switched off or set to high. "Small" is only the product name; this is a large model.

name: Mistral Medium 3.5 128B
license_note: Companies with more than US$20 million global revenue a month, and their employees, may not use it without a commercial licence from Mistral. Check before using it in a large company.

arch_detail.kv_note: Dense transformer; every one of 88 layers stores K and V, so the cache is large (352 KB per token).

good_for: The model behind Mistral's own coding assistant: one model for chat, reasoning and programming.
weak_at: The licence forbids use by companies with more than US$20 million revenue a month.
notes: The released files are already 8-bit, so higher precision settings add nothing. It is slow on Macs and other computers where the processor and graphics share memory, because all 128 billion parameters are used for every word. After release Mistral fixed a setting that hurt quality on long inputs, so download older copies again.

name: Apertus 1.5 70B
lab: Swiss AI Initiative (EPFL, ETH Zurich, CSCS)
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Same language-model architecture as Apertus 1.0 70B (80 layers, 8 KV heads); taken from the 1.0 config because the 1.5 config is gated.

good_for: The largest fully open European model, with public training data, many languages, and image and audio input.
weak_at: Less capable than similar-size rivals, and no ready-made download for local apps.
notes: You must accept the terms on Hugging Face before downloading; approval is automatic. It is not confirmed that llama.cpp supports version 1.5; the older text-only Apertus 1.0 has compact files from the community. Mainly useful where you must know where the training data came from, for example for transparency under the EU AI Act.

name: Step 3.7 Flash
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: 12 of 45 layers are full attention (8 KV groups); 33 sliding layers (512-token window) add a fixed ~69 MB. 288 experts per MoE layer.

good_for: Very good at searching with pictures and reading dense reports and app screens, built for heavy use.
weak_at: Always reasons before answering, which adds delay.
notes: StepFun publishes its own compact files as well as 8-bit and 4-bit versions, and lists llama.cpp as supported.

name: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
license_note: Commercial use needs a one-time notice to MiniMax and a "Built with MiniMax M3.1-Flash" credit. Products with more than US$20 million revenue a year need written permission first.

arch_detail.kv_note: Every layer caches K and V (4 KV heads); MiniMax Sparse Attention reads only selected 128-token blocks, which cuts compute, not cache size. A small index key per token is also cached (not counted).

good_for: Strong at operating a computer, long tool-using jobs and security work, and it handles very long inputs.
weak_at: Any business use requires notifying MiniMax first.
notes: The released files are already compressed (mostly 4-bit), so higher precision settings add nothing. It needs a test version of llama.cpp that was not yet part of the main release in November 2026. Ollama offers it only as a cloud model, which runs on Ollama's servers.

name: GLM-5.3-Flash
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the copyright notice.

arch_detail.kv_note: 34 of 45 layers are Kimi-style linear attention (KDA, fixed state); 11 are DeepSeek-sparse-attention layers with an MLA cache of one 512-dim latent per token (no RoPE part).

good_for: Close to Z.ai's flagship at programming and tool use while much cheaper to run, and it also reads images.
weak_at: Always reasons before answering.
notes: The released files are already 8-bit (about 321 GB), so higher precision settings add nothing. It has run in llama.cpp since about 1 October 2026, and long working sessions need very little extra memory for the conversation. Ollama offers it only as a cloud model, which runs on Ollama's servers.

name: MiMo-V2.6-Flash
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the copyright notice.

arch_detail.kv_note: 9 of 48 layers are full attention (4 KV heads, K 192 + V 128 dims); 39 sliding layers (128-token window, 8 KV heads) add a fixed ~26 MB.

good_for: Takes text, images, video and sound in one model, and people rate its chat answers highly for the cost.
weak_at: Few people have tested it on their own computers yet.
notes: The released files are already compressed (mostly 4-bit), so higher precision settings add nothing. Standard llama.cpp appears to support it, since the llama.cpp team publishes compact files for it. There are two trained versions; the compact files linked here are for the main one (-RL).

name: Qwen3.5 397B-A17B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: 15 of 60 layers use full attention (2 KV heads); the rest are Gated DeltaNet. 512 experts, 10 routed + 1 shared.

good_for: The largest freely licensed Qwen, with wide general knowledge and about 200 languages, for very large computers.
weak_at: Older generation, and not in Ollama for local use.
notes: Qwen publishes an official 4-bit version.

name: Inkling 2 Small
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: 8 of 48 layers are global (8 KV heads); 40 local layers (1024-token window) add a fixed ~168 MB. 384 experts, 8 active, no shared expert.

good_for: A freely licensed model close to the best open models, and especially strong at hard programming problems.
weak_at: Mainly English, and needs a test version of the usual local software.
notes: It was trained in 4-bit and the released files are already 4-bit (about 394 GB), so higher precision settings add nothing. It needs a test version of llama.cpp that is not yet part of the main release. You can turn its thinking down, but it is not documented whether it can be switched off completely.

name: Inkling 2 Mini
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices. The lab also publishes a usage policy (for example, no automated decisions about people's rights) that is worth reading.

arch_detail.kv_note: 24 layers of weights, of which the middle 12 run three times per token (48 layer passes). 4 layers are global attention; counting the three passes of the two in the loop, that is 8 global passes with 8 KV heads. The 20 local layers (1024-token window) add a fixed amount of about 168 MB. 128 experts, 8 used per token. If the repeated passes share one cache, the real figure is lower.

good_for: A small model for coding by itself and using tools; it also reads images and fits one 32 GB machine.
weak_at: Worse than Qwen3.8 27B at following long, detailed instructions, and it can get stuck in long reasoning loops.
notes: The released files are already compressed (about 20 GB), so higher precision settings add nothing; Ollama has it. Some middle layers run three times for every word, so for speed it behaves like a 5.4 billion parameter model, more than the 3.4 billion active figure on the lab's page. Limit the output length: the lab warns of long reasoning loops, and thinking cannot be switched off completely.

name: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (1017)
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the copyright notice.

arch_detail.kv_note: Compressed Sparse Attention 2: 20-layer encoder + 20-layer decoder, KV shared and reused across layers and stored in FP4. DeepSeek reports 890 bytes per token for the global cache; the FP16 figure here is that number scaled from 4.5 to 16 bits. Sliding-window KV is extra but bounded.

good_for: One of the best open models for long programming sessions on its own, with very little extra memory for long chats.
weak_at: Needs a test version of the usual local software.
notes: The 763B figure includes about 196B of lookup tables that can stay on the SSD; the main part that has to sit in fast memory is about 552B. The released files are already compressed (mostly 4-bit), and it needs a test version of llama.cpp that is not yet part of the main release. Ollama offers it only as a cloud model, and DeepSeek provides no standard chat template, which some local apps expect.

name: Ling-3.1-flash (1019)
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the copyright notice.

arch_detail.kv_note: 63 Kimi Delta Attention layers (fixed state) + 9 gated MLA layers, each caching a 512-dim latent plus 64-dim RoPE key.

good_for: Strong at science problems and at office-style jobs done step by step with tools; free for business use.
weak_at: Text only, with little guidance on running it locally.
notes: The released files are already 8-bit, so higher precision settings add nothing. Community compact files exist, but llama.cpp support has not been confirmed otherwise. It reads 262,000 tokens by default; the lab says up to 1 million.

name: GLM-5.3
license_note: Commercial use is allowed. Only companies that sell model access as an online service and have more than US$10 billion revenue a year must pass a security review by Z.ai first.

arch_detail.kv_note: MLA with DeepSeek Sparse Attention: each of 78 layers caches a 512-dim latent + 64-dim RoPE key. 21 layers also cache a 128-dim indexer key (~5 KB/token extra, not counted).

good_for: Z.ai's flagship for long, multi-step programming jobs, and among the best open models at working in a terminal.
weak_at: Text only, and needs server-sized memory.
notes: The released files are already 8-bit (about 753 GB), so higher precision settings add nothing. It thinks at the highest level by default; you can set it to low or high, and a separate setting gives plain chat. Ollama offers it only as a cloud model, which runs on Ollama's servers.

name: Muse Spark Open 816B-A42B
license_note: Commercial use is allowed if you show "Built with Muse Spark Open" and follow Meta's usage policy. Companies that sell model access as an online service and have more than US$20 million revenue need a separate agreement.

arch_detail.kv_note: 16 of 62 layers are global (16 KV heads x 64 dims); 46 sliding layers (2048-token window) add a fixed ~386 MB. 256 experts, 8 active.

good_for: Meta's largest open model: understands text, images, video and sound, and handles long programming tasks.
weak_at: The licence requires a "Built with Muse Spark Open" credit.
notes: Meta approves each download request on Hugging Face by hand. Meta says its 4-bit version needs about 700 GB of graphics memory. Standard llama.cpp appears to support it, since the llama.cpp team publishes compact files for it; Ollama offers it only as a cloud model.

name: Nemotron 3 Ultra 550B-A55B
license_note: Permissive: commercial use is allowed with no limits on revenue or user numbers. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Mamba-2 hybrid: 12 of 108 blocks are attention (2 KV heads); 48 Mamba-2 blocks keep fixed state; 48 LatentMoE blocks (512 experts, 22 active).

good_for: A very large model whose weights, training data and methods are all public.
weak_at: Text only, and weaker at programming than the top Chinese models.
notes: NVIDIA offers a 4-bit version, and long conversations need very little extra memory for a model this size. Supported languages: English, French, Spanish, Italian, German, Japanese, Hindi, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese and Chinese. Ollama offers it only as a cloud model, which runs on Ollama's servers.

name: Mistral Large 4 (1T-A52B)
license_note: Commercial use is allowed, including inside your own products. Any company that sells model access as an online service needs a separate commercial licence, whatever its size; use inside your own company is exempt.

arch_detail.kv_note: MLA with sparse indexed attention: 72 layers, but only 63 store their own latent (512 + 64 RoPE dims); the rest reuse another layer's cache. Indexer keys (~11 KB/token) not counted.

good_for: Mistral's European flagship, fluent in over 160 languages including all EU ones; Mistral highlights law, finance and security.
weak_at: Companies selling AI access as a service need a paid licence.
notes: Standard llama.cpp appears to support it, since the llama.cpp team publishes compact files for it. You can set how much it thinks: low, medium or high. It was trained in Mistral's own data centres in the EU.

name: Kimi K2.7 Code
license_note: Commercial use is allowed. Products with more than 100 million monthly users or US$20 million monthly revenue must display "Kimi K2.7 Code" in their user interface.

arch_detail.kv_note: DeepSeek-V3-style MLA: each of 61 layers caches a 512-dim latent + 64-dim RoPE key. 384 experts, 8 active.

good_for: Specialised for long programming jobs, and thinks more briefly than the Kimi model it is built on.
weak_at: Always thinks before answering; there is no quick-reply mode.
notes: The released files are already 4-bit and were trained that way, so a 4-bit compact file loses almost nothing and higher precision settings add nothing. Standard llama.cpp supports it. Ollama offers it only as a cloud model, which runs on Ollama's servers.

name: Kimi K3.1 Pro
license_note: Commercial use is allowed. Companies that sell model access as an online service and earn more than US$20 million in 12 months need a separate agreement. Products with more than 100 million monthly users or US$20 million monthly revenue must show the model name; use inside your own company is exempt.

arch_detail.kv_note: 69 Kimi Delta Attention layers (fixed state) + 24 gated DeepSeek-sparse-attention layers with an MLA cache (512-dim latent + 64-dim RoPE key; config also sets mla_use_nope, so the RoPE part may be absent). Indexer keys not counted.

good_for: The most capable open model in November 2026, for complex multi-step tasks, programming and work with pictures.
weak_at: Enormous, and common local apps cannot run it yet.
notes: The released files are already 4-bit (about 1.5 TB), so higher precision settings add nothing. It does not run in llama.cpp yet, because its design differs from the older Kimi K3; Kimi K3 itself has compact files if you want to run a Kimi model locally today. Ollama offers it only as a cloud model, which runs on Ollama's servers.

name: Qwen3 Embedding 0.6B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Embedding model: no KV cache is kept between requests; memory scales with batch size and input length.

good_for: A small, fast way to make documents searchable by meaning in many languages; runs fine without a graphics card.
weak_at: Text only, and less accurate than the 8B version.
notes: Qwen publishes its own compact files. You can add a short instruction to each search query, and its search vectors (up to 1,024 numbers each) can be shortened to save storage.

name: Qwen3 Embedding 8B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Embedding model: no KV cache is kept between requests.

good_for: Very accurate search by meaning across many languages and code; it was the top multilingual search model when released.
weak_at: Slow and heavy for preparing large document collections for search.
notes: Its search vectors (up to 4,096 numbers each) can be shortened to save storage. For the best results when a chat model answers from your documents, pair it with Qwen3 Reranker. Newer versions that also handle images exist (Qwen3-VL-Embedding, January 2026).

name: EmbeddingGemma 2
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Embedding model built on Gemma 4 blocks; no KV cache is kept between requests.

good_for: Lets you search text, images, video and audio together, and its text-only part is very small.
weak_at: Each item you add to the search can be at most about 6,000 words.
notes: The image and audio parts load only when needed, so text search uses just the 270M text part; Ollama also has a text-only version (embeddinggemma-2:270m). Its search vectors have 768 numbers and can be shortened to 128. It covers more than 100 languages.

name: Qwen3 Reranker 0.6B
license_note: Permissive: companies of any size may use it commercially. If you pass the model files on, include the licence and notices.

arch_detail.kv_note: Reranker (cross-encoder scoring); no KV cache is kept between requests.

good_for: Re-orders search results so the most relevant passages reach the chat model first; small enough for a normal processor.
weak_at: Not in Ollama, so it needs other tools to run.
notes: It scores how well each passage matches a question, to sort the results a search model has already found. The llama.cpp server runs it with its reranking option turned on. Larger 4B and 8B versions are more accurate.
